title: Search engines post-ChatGPT: How generative artificial intelligence could make search less reliable
extended_summary:
This commentary examines how generative AI is being integrated into search engines and argues that this shift can reduce the reliability of search results. The paper focuses on problems such as hallucinated content, decontextualized quotations, incorrect or misleading citations, hidden provenance, and the amplification of bias when large language models are used to synthesize answers rather than simply rank documents.

The authors illustrate these concerns with examples from contemporary generative search systems, including Google’s Search Generative Experience, Perplexity AI, Arc Search, BingChat, and You.com. They show that small query changes and typos can trigger confidently written but factually incorrect answers, and that these systems may fabricate support for claims or misattribute source material. They frame this behavior as an instance of retrieval-augmented generation that is not sufficiently protected by guardrails, especially when the system prefers generating an answer over refusing to answer.

The paper does not study a K–12 population or an educational intervention; it is a position/commentary piece about information systems. Its main conclusion is that generative search trades efficiency and convenience for reduced reliability, lower transparency, and increased risk of biased or misleading outputs. The authors call for stronger mitigation techniques, better refusal behavior, more attention to provenance and verifiability, and further research on how users interpret and trust generative search results.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI / large language model systems that produce natural-language text, sometimes used in retrieval-augmented or question-answering interfaces.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a commentary on generative search systems and uses examples from ChatGPT-like, Perplexity AI, BingChat, Google SGE, YouChat, and Arc Search to illustrate risks in generated search responses; it does not evaluate a single educational tool.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a commentary/opinion piece rather than an empirical study, meta-analysis, or systematic review. It discusses risks and mechanisms of generative search systems but reports no original study design, sample, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No effect sizes, samples, or outcome measurements are reported, so there is no empirical impact estimate to assess. The paper is useful for conceptual understanding of GenAI risks, but not for evidence of instructional or learning impact.
